observations.observation: Equality for rank-three cyclic factors 3 times powers of two. Does not settle n15/n20.
D(C2 + C2m + C2mn)=2m+2mn; first invariant factor is 2, not n.
D4(C5^3)=30 and Dk(C5^3)=5k+10 for k>=2; computation-dependent source statement. No ancillary certificate replay. Same work also catalogued historically as SRC-0015.

D(Cn^3)<=4n-P(n)-2, P largest prime-power component; n15 gives 53, n20 gives 73, weaker than historical intervals. Statement read with pypdf from in-memory bytes after web PDF fetch failures; no PDF retained, no proof or formalization replay. Same work historically SRC-0016.
General bound D(G)<4.86 exp(G) log|G|/log exp(G); D~D* for almost all groups in the stated counting model. No exact rank-three target value.
For r>=5,m>=2, F=C_m^(r-4)+C_3m^3+C_6m has D-D*>=m. General upper bound D(G)<=16 rank(G) exp(G)/5. v1 only gave rank>=8. Neither construction is homocyclic rank three.
For C2^3+C2n, nu=d=d* at odd n>=3 and nu=d-1 otherwise. Further values for C2^r+C2n, r=5,6. Refutes a missing-sums invariant conjecture, not homocyclic rank-three equality.
For fixed nontrivial odd p-group H, D(H+C2^r)=D*(H+C2^r)+(D(H)-1)log2(r)+O_H(1); exact intervals for C3+C2^r. Growing rank, not an exact n15/n20 theorem.
